signature: SUBROUTINE DLASY2( LTRANL, LTRANR, ISGN, N1, N2, TL, LDTL, TR,

params.name: isgn
params.reference: On entry, `ISGN` specifies the sign of the equation as described before. `ISGN` may only be 1 or -1.

params.name: n1
params.reference: On entry, `N1` specifies the order of matrix `TL`. `N1` may only be 0, 1 or 2.

params.name: n2
params.reference: On entry, `N2` specifies the order of matrix `TR`. `N2` may only be 0, 1 or 2.

params.name: TL
params.reference: On entry, `TL` contains an `N1` by `N1` matrix.

params.name: ldtl
params.reference: The leading dimension of the matrix `TL`. $\mathrm{LDTL} \ge \max (1,N_{1})$.

params.name: TR
params.reference: On entry, `TR` contains an `N2` by `N2` matrix.

params.name: ldtr
params.reference: The leading dimension of the matrix `TR`. $\mathrm{LDTR} \ge \max (1,N_{2})$.

params.name: B
params.reference: On entry, the `N1` by `N2` matrix B contains the right-hand side of the equation.

params.name: ldb
params.reference: The leading dimension of the matrix B. $\mathrm{LDB} \ge \max (1,N_{1})$.

params.name: scale
params.reference: On exit, `SCALE` contains the scale factor. `SCALE` is chosen less than or equal to 1 to prevent the solution overflowing.

params.name: X
params.reference: On exit, X contains the `N1` by `N2` solution.

params.name: ldx
params.reference: The leading dimension of the matrix X. $\mathrm{LDX} \ge \max (1,N_{1})$.

params.name: xnorm
params.reference: On exit, `XNORM` is the infinity-norm of the solution.

params.name: info
params.reference:
On exit, `INFO` is set to

-   0: successful exit.
-   1: `TL` and `TR` have too close eigenvalues, so `TL` or `TR` is perturbed to get a nonsingular equation.

NOTE: In the interests of speed, this routine does not

check the inputs for errors.
